newsitem.title: FRANCE: Monaco premier quits for new job in France.
newsitem.headline: Monaco premier quits for new job in France.

text.p: Prince Rainier of Monaco has agreed to let his French prime minister step down and return home to take up a new post handling French relations with Latin America, the French Foreign Ministry said on Friday.
"The Prince of Monaco has...expressed his thanks and satisfaction to Mr Paul Dijoud about the job he has done over the past two years," ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
Monaco officials said it was not yet known who would replace Dijoud, officially titled Minister of State and the head of a five-strong cabinet in the tiny principality.
Rainier, who rules over a population of just 30,000 and less than two square km (one square mile) of territory nestled on the French Riviera, chooses cabinet members from a list proposed by Paris.

Rummelhardt said French President Jacques Chirac and Foreign Minister Herve de Charette had asked Dijoud to carry out "an important mission...in the framework of relations in Latin America and ahead of the coming visit by Jacques Chirac to this region which is growing strongly."

The announcement of Dijoud's departure comes just two days after Monaco launched a 10-month birthday party to fete the 700th anniversary of the state, known more for its glamorous royal family than its politics.
